rule: feature-renderer-frontmatter — a document-LEADING `---`-delimited YAML frontmatter block (RENDERER_PIPELINE_VERSION 1.1.0+) is scanned (never YAML-parsed) into an ordered `crowiFrontmatter{entries: {key,value}[]}` node instead of rendering as a thematicBreak + paragraph. A mid-document `---` is unaffected (stays a thematicBreak). Malformed/oversized blocks fall back to a `code` node instead (covered at the unit level by core/frontmatter.test.ts, not pinned here — a fallback case's downstream shiki-highlighted output is a generated byte string, same exclusion as code.json).
why: crowiFrontmatter is a new entry in RENDERED_AST_NODE_DEFS (feature-renderer-frontmatter) — this corpus case fixes its wire shape (no data, no children, ordered string-only entries) for both the api producer and the CrowiKit iOS consumer, and doubles as the AC-10 pin that a frontmatter-bearing document round-trips correctly under the 1.1.0 pipeline.
consumerContract: The api jest driver asserts the PRODUCER side (markdown → expectedAst via runPipeline with an empty registry, and storedAst/expectedAst → expectedEnvelope via sanitizeAst). The CrowiKit XCTest asserts the CONSUMER side (its sanitize-walker mirror over storedAst/expectedAst, and its strict envelope decoder over expectedEnvelope). The Swift consumer is wired up in Phase 4 (apps/apple lives on the feature-ios-app/impl branch).
exclusions: Plugin-dispatch output byte strings (Mermaid / PlantUML / link-card / shiki generated HTML) are deliberately NOT pinned by this corpus — packages/e2e/tests/renderer-plugins.spec.ts owns that coverage against a live server. A malformed/oversized frontmatter block falls back to a `code` node that the LATER core syntax-highlight transform turns into shiki-generated `html` (same byte-string problem as code.json), so that fallback path is intentionally left to core/frontmatter.test.ts's isolated unit coverage instead of this corpus.

cases.name: frontmatter-basic
cases.why: the happy path: a document-leading frontmatter block becomes crowiFrontmatter with ordered entries, and the body renders normally right after it — no thematicBreak, no stray break nodes from the frontmatter markers/content
